question: Do explicit residual-regime decomposition and direct full-field horse-vs-horse comparison jointly break the L1 top1 podium ceiling?

architectures.RESIDUAL_REGIME_DIRECT: core4 + decomposed V1 residual regimes, direct LambdaRank
architectures.FULL_PAIRWISE_BASE: all horses compared pair-by-pair from compact pre-race horse features
architectures.FULL_PAIRWISE_REGIME: all horses compared pair-by-pair with the same residual-regime state added

pairwise.coverage: all unordered horse pairs in every race; 18 horses = 153 pair comparisons

targets.PAIR_FINISH: A finishes ahead of B for all non-dead-heat train pairs
targets.PAIR_TOP3: A is podium and B is not, trained only across the podium boundary

pairwise.ranking: mean predicted pairwise win probability across all opponents
pairwise.anti_row_leak: pair orientation comes from horse_id sort and deterministic alternating direction, never result/source row order
pairwise.base_feature_selection: train-only, label-free coverage filter; maximum 96 compact horse-level numeric features

strictness: Every history/regime feature is shifted by >=1 horse race date.
Pairwise A/B orientation is independent of finish-table row order.
Two prior calendar years train each next unknown year, 2021-2025.
No odds or popularity are used.
promotion_rule: Require >=2.0pp pooled top1_top3 uplift vs baseline direct and no fold worse than -0.5pp.
